title: Adoption mode becomes a checked key on every osf.toml reader
summary: This change introduces a top-level `adoption_mode` key in a repository's own `osf.toml` and funnels every reader of that file through a single parse step, `config::repo_document`, which refuses an unsupported value. Previously each reader (`review_config`, `agents_config`, `changeset_risk::hot_paths`, `review_context::scan_config`) read and parsed the file on its own and silently fell back to defaults on a read or parse failure; now a missing file still yields defaults, but an unreadable, malformed, or unsupported-mode file is an error that names the key and the supported values. The layered `config::load` and the `--gate` load share the same parser, so `osf config show`, `lint writing --gate`, `agents list`, `review run` and `changeset risk` all stop on a bad mode. A new `require_adoption_mode` helper lets a command declare which modes it supports; no command calls it yet.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: command dispatch
nodes.summary: The binary that runs config show, lint, agents, review and changeset subcommands. Every one of these now reaches the adoption-mode check through the config layer.

nodes.label: osf config show
nodes.subtitle: layered load
nodes.summary: Loads the layered configuration. It now refuses an unsupported adoption_mode in the repository's own osf.toml, and drops the key before merging so it never trips deny_unknown_fields.

nodes.label: lint writing --gate
nodes.subtitle: gate_must_explain_names
nodes.summary: The gate reads the repository's own osf.toml for writing.must_explain_names. It takes no setting from the file but now still refuses an unsupported adoption_mode, because it shares the parser.

nodes.label: osf agents list
nodes.subtitle: agents_config
nodes.summary: Lists configured agents. It now stops on an unsupported adoption_mode rather than reading the [agents] table regardless.

nodes.label: osf review run
nodes.subtitle: review_config
nodes.summary: Runs the review pipeline. Its review_config read now goes through the shared parser and refuses an unsupported adoption_mode.

nodes.label: osf changeset risk
nodes.subtitle: assess
nodes.summary: Assesses a changeset. Its hot_paths reader now returns a Result and propagates a bad adoption_mode up through assess.

nodes.label: config::repo_document
nodes.subtitle: fn repo_document(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<toml::Value>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The one entry point for reading a repository's own osf.toml outside the layered load. Returns None when the file is absent, and an error when it cannot be read, is not valid TOML, or names an unsupported adoption_mode.

nodes.label: parse_repo_document
nodes.subtitle: fn parse_repo_document(text: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<toml::Value, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Parses osf.toml text and checks its adoption_mode. Shared by repo_document and the layered load, so no reader can skip the check.

nodes.label: AdoptionMode
nodes.subtitle: enum AdoptionMode { PrivateFactoryRepo }
nodes.summary: The supported placement shapes. One variant exists so far, private-factory-repo; a later mode adds a variant and a name in AdoptionMode::ALL.

nodes.label: config::adoption_mode
nodes.subtitle: fn adoption_mode(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<AdoptionMode>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Reads the top-level adoption_mode key, or None when the file or the key is absent. An unsupported value is an error naming the key and the supported values.

nodes.label: config::require_adoption_mode
nodes.subtitle: fn require_adoption_mode(root, command, supported) -> Result<AdoptionMode, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The mode a command needs: reads the key and checks it against the modes the command supports. An unset key is refused too, so a command never runs on a guessed mode. No command calls it yet.

nodes.label: config::load
nodes.subtitle: layered loader
nodes.summary: The layered configuration loader. It now parses through parse_repo_document and removes the adoption_mode key before merging, so the key is checked but never merged into the layered struct.

nodes.label: config::review_config
nodes.subtitle: [review] table reader
nodes.summary: Reads the [review] table. It now delegates the read and parse to repo_document, so an unsupported adoption_mode stops it instead of being ignored.

nodes.label: config::agents_config
nodes.subtitle: [agents] table reader
nodes.summary: Reads the [agents] table. It now delegates to repo_document and so refuses an unsupported adoption_mode.

nodes.label: changeset_risk::hot_paths
nodes.subtitle: fn hot_paths(root: &Path) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>
nodes.summary: Reads [review] hot_paths for the risk signal. It now returns a Result and goes through repo_document, so a malformed or unsupported-mode osf.toml stops the risk assessment instead of silently disabling the signal.

nodes.label: review_context::scan_config
nodes.subtitle: fn scan_config(config_root: &Path) -> Result<ScanConfig, String>
nodes.summary: Reads the [scan] table for redaction rules. It now returns a Result and goes through repo_document, so redaction stops on a bad osf.toml rather than falling back to compiled defaults.

nodes.label: review_context::redact_secrets
nodes.subtitle: redaction entry point
nodes.summary: Redacts lens context. It now propagates the scan_config error, so an unsupported adoption_mode stops redaction rather than running with defaults.

nodes.label: osf.toml
nodes.subtitle: adoption_mode = "private-factory-repo"
nodes.summary: The adopter's repository config. It gains a top-level adoption_mode string; leaving it out means no mode is read, and an unknown value stops osf.

nodes.label: adoption_mode integration tests
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/adoption_mode.rs
nodes.summary: End-to-end tests that an unsupported mode stops config show, the writing gate and agents list, naming the key and every supported value, and that a supported mode loads.

edges.label: every reader
edges.summary: The change's core move: every command that reads the repository's own osf.toml now goes through one parse step that checks adoption_mode.

edges.label: read_to_string
edges.summary: Reads the file, returning None only when it is absent; any other read error is an error.
Delegates parsing and the adoption_mode check to the shared parser.

edges.label: adoption_mode_of
edges.summary: Checks the parsed document's adoption_mode against the supported variants.
Reads the key through the shared parse step.
Checks the configured mode against the modes a command supports, refusing an unset key.
The layered load now shares the parser, so it refuses an unsupported mode and drops the key before merging.
review_config now delegates its read and parse to repo_document.
agents_config now delegates its read and parse to repo_document.
hot_paths now returns a Result and propagates a bad adoption_mode instead of defaulting to an empty list.
scan_config now returns a Result and propagates a bad adoption_mode instead of falling back to compiled defaults.
redact_secrets now propagates the scan_config error.
config show renders the layered configuration.
The gate takes no setting from the file but now still refuses an unsupported adoption_mode through the shared parser.
assess now propagates the hot_paths error with `?`.
The new integration tests drive the CLI with a bad and a good adoption_mode.

chips.label: Commands that stop on a bad mode

views.title: Adoption mode check across osf commands
views.summary: Every command that reads the repository's own osf.toml now reaches one parse step, config::repo_document, which checks adoption_mode. The layered load and the gate share its parser; the risk and review-context readers now propagate its errors instead of defaulting.

views.title: Config layer internals
views.summary: Inside the config layer: repo_document reads the file and delegates to parse_repo_document, which checks the parsed document against AdoptionMode. adoption_mode and require_adoption_mode are the read and require helpers a command uses.
